LONDON – British novelist Frederick Forsyth, who authored best-selling thrillers such as The Day Of The Jackal and The Dogs Of War, has died aged 86, his publisher said.
A former correspondent for Reuters and the BBC, and an informant for Britain’s MI6 foreign spy agency, Forsyth made his name by using his experiences as a reporter in Paris to pen the story of a failed assassination plot on French president Charles de Gaulle.
The Day Of The Jackal, in which an English assassin is hired by French paramilitaries angry at de Gaulle’s withdrawal from Algeria, was published in 1971 after Forsyth found himself penniless in London.
